messages.content: Calculate the slope gradient in degree between two points on a landscape with coordinates (40.7128, -74.0060) and (34.0522, -118.2437).

function.name: calculate_slope_gradient
function.description: Calculate the slope gradient between two geographical coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

point1.description: The geographic coordinates for the first point [Latitude, Longitude].

point2.description: The geographic coordinates for the second point [Latitude, Longitude].

unit.description: The unit for the slope gradient. Default is 'degree'.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I can’t compute a slope gradient (in degrees) from just latitude/longitude coordinates.  
A slope gradient is defined as the vertical rise divided by the horizontal run, usually expressed as an angle:

\[
\theta = \arctan\!\left(\frac{\Delta h}{d_{\text{horizontal}}}\right)
\]

where  
* \(\Delta h\) is the difference in elevation (height) between the two points, and  
* \(d_{\text{horizontal}}\) is the horizontal distance between them (often the ground‑surface distance).

With only the geographic coordinates \((40.7128^\circ N, -74.0060^\circ W)\) and \((34.0522^\circ N, -118.2437^\circ W)\) you can calculate the great‑circle distance between the points, but you still need the elevations at each location to determine the vertical change. Without that information the slope gradient is indeterminate.

If you can provide the elevations (or the vertical difference) for the two points, I can calculate the slope gradient in degrees for you.
